title: grid_check_is_clear assertion failure (SIGABRT) entering copy-mode on macOS (master)
body:
### Issue description

Following up on #5314, where @participant1 noted the macOS grid checks stay in until this bug is found and that `grid_check_is_clear` is the important one — we hit that assertion twice in normal desktop use and have crash reports.

**Build:** tmux master via Homebrew `--HEAD`, commit `9180356`, built 2026-07-06 (`tmux -V` reported `next-3.8`)
**Platform:** macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), Apple Silicon (Mac mini)

Two SIGABRTs four days apart (2026-07-06 20:57, 2026-07-10 09:51) with an **identical faulting stack** — the assert fires while entering copy-mode, when the pane screen is cloned:

```
#0 libsystem_kernel.dylib!__pthread_kill+8
#1 libsystem_pthread.dylib!pthread_kill+296
#2 libsystem_c.dylib!abort+148
#3 libsystem_c.dylib!__assert_rtn+284
#4 tmux!grid_check_is_clear.cold.4+36      (second crash: .cold.5)
#5 tmux!grid_check_is_clear+144            (second crash: +148)
#6 tmux!grid_create+96
#7 tmux!screen_init+32
#8 tmux!window_copy_clone_screen+220
#9 tmux!window_copy_init+72
#10 tmux!window_pane_set_mode+196
#11 tmux!cmd_copy_mode_exec+384
#12 tmux!cmdq_next+844
#13 tmux!server_loop+80
```

Both reports carry the ASI annotation `libsystem_c.dylib: crashed on child side of fork pre-exec` (verbatim; leaving interpretation to you).

**Workload context** (in case it helps narrow the search): this server sees a lot of scripted layout churn — windows created by scripts (`new-window`, several `split-window -l <cells>` in quick succession, explicit `resize-window -x -y`), `window-size manual`, hooks that immediately `resize-window` new windows again, and panes running full-screen TUIs producing heavy output. Copy-mode is entered frequently for scrollback; per the stack, the abort happens at copy-mode entry, so the grid presumably went inconsistent some time earlier during the layout churn.

Possibly related: on 2026-07-12 the same build's server exited abruptly twice (no crash report, socket left behind), each time within a minute of a scripted layout rebuild. Consistent with a `fatal()` exit path, but we could not confirm it is the same root cause.

We have since moved this machine back to 3.7b, so I can't provide `-vv` logs of the crash itself. The two full `.ips` crash reports are available on request, and I'm happy to run diagnostics or an instrumented build if that helps.

comments.author: participant1
participant1
comments.body:
OK best theory is that there is a UAF that corrupts a page the allocator has already zeroed. It seems likely it must be temporally fairly close because otherwise we should probably have had at least one crash somewhere else, but they have been entirely consistent.

I think the best approach may be to enable ASAN by default at least for macOS builds.

If anything obvious is wrong let me know, or if you see this bug again. If it crashes, look for `/tmp/tmux-asan*` logs.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I built the ASAN-by-default master and gave it a soak on macOS ARM. Summary: the ASAN build compiles, links, and runs cleanly; I could not reproduce the copy-mode crash under it yet; and I have one new data point from a stable-3.7b crash today that lines up with the use-after-free theory from the `free()` side.

## ASAN build: compiles, links, runs

- HEAD `42b3ea0d7411acb4cd0357a3c2829d986b455918` (`tmux next-3.8`), which includes `330bedfb` ("Build with ASAN on macOS by default") — confirmed ancestor via `git merge-base --is-ancestor`.
- macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), Apple Silicon (Mac mini).
- `autogen.sh` → `./configure --enable-utf8proc` → `make` builds clean with no extra deps beyond the usual autoconf/automake/pkgconf/libevent/ncurses/utf8proc. A bare `./configure` defaults ASAN on for darwin now (`configure.ac`); I also passed `--enable-asan` explicitly, which is redundant here.
- ASAN is actually linked in, not just requested: compile flags show `-DASAN -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer`, `otool -L` shows `libclang_rt.asan_osx_dynamic.dylib`, and `__asan_default_options` is compiled into the binary returning `log_path=/tmp/tmux-asan:log_exe_name=1` — so a crash will drop `/tmp/tmux-asan.<pid>` with no env needed.
- Runs normally: sessions, splits, and copy-mode enter/exit all behave under ASAN. Nothing obviously wrong.

## Soak (no repro yet)

Scripted stress on isolated sockets, four workloads × 3 rounds × 7 min (≈84 soak-minutes, ~2870 iterations total), each entering copy-mode frequently since that's where it aborts:

- copy-mode churn — big scrollback bursts (2k–10k lines) into panes, then rapid copy-mode enter / scroll (history-top, page-down, halfpage-up) / cancel loops, with periodic alternate-screen toggles (529 iters)
- history flood — wide CJK/emoji + 500-col wrapping + burst output, interleaved with `clear-history` and `new-window`/history-limit churn (1071 iters)
- resize storm — `resize-window -x/-y` between wide and very narrow, `resize-pane` churn, layout cycling (470 iters)
- pane lifecycle — split/kill/break/join/swap/respawn-pane churn plus new-window/kill-window, copy-mode on survivors after each structural change (798 iters)

All rounds exited 0. No ASAN reports, no `SERVER-DIED`/abrupt exits, `/tmp/tmux-asan.*` stayed empty. So this doesn't rule the bug out — it likely needs a churn pattern/timing my profiles didn't hit — but the ASAN build itself is fine to ship as the default. I'll keep an ASAN build in rotation for this workload and post the `/tmp/tmux-asan.<pid>` log the moment it fires.

## New data point: stable 3.7b crash today, `free()` side

After the earlier crashes I moved this machine back to 3.7b (brew), and it aborted again today entering copy-mode — same clone entry, but this time the malloc abort is on the free side rather than your `grid_check_is_clear` assert. `procPath` in the report is the Homebrew 3.7b binary. Faulting thread is the main server thread:

```
abort
malloc_vreport
malloc_report
___BUG_IN_CLIENT_OF_LIBMALLOC_POINTER_BEING_FREED_WAS_NOT_ALLOCATED
grid_free_line
grid_clear_lines
screen_reinit
window_copy_clone_screen
window_copy_init
window_pane_set_mode
cmd_copy_mode_exec
cmdq_next
server_loop
proc_loop
server_start
client_main
```

So on 3.7b (no APPLE `grid_check_is_clear` assert compiled in) the same underlying grid corruption surfaces as libmalloc rejecting a free of a pointer that "was not allocated", inside `grid_clear_lines` → `grid_free_line` during `window_copy_clone_screen`. Same copy-mode clone trigger, corruption showing up on the free side instead of the allocation side — which I think is consistent with your "a use-after-free corrupted a page the allocator already touched" theory: the alloc-side path sees a page that isn't zero, the free-side path sees a line pointer that isn't a real allocation. It also confirms this isn't master-only; 3.7b hits it too.

(Same `libsystem_c.dylib: "crashed on child side of fork pre-exec"` annotation as the earlier reports, but the faulting thread is clearly the main server thread in copy-mode.)

Happy to attach the full `.ips` if useful, and I'll follow up with `/tmp/tmux-asan*` if the ASAN build catches it.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
New data point from master, this time with a full ASan report: a heap-use-after-free of a client's `cwd` string, caught on master `f07ea87e` (next-3.8), macOS 26.x (Darwin 25.5) arm64, ASAN build (the darwin configure default).

**What ASan caught**: `cmd_source_file_exec` read 2 bytes of freed memory via `strlen`. The freed string was allocated by `server_client_dispatch` (`xstrdup`) and freed by `server_client_lost`.

**Source-level walk (at f07ea87e)**:

- free side: `server_client_lost` does `free((void *)c->cwd);` (server-client.c:541) and does not NULL the pointer.
- use side: `cmd_source_file_exec` calls `server_client_get_cwd(c, NULL)` (cmd-source-file.c:201), which returns the dangling `c->cwd` (server-client.c:2972), and `cmd_source_file_quote_for_glob` immediately does `xmalloc(2 * strlen(path) + 1)` (cmd-source-file.c:147) — that `strlen` is the faulting read.
- the 2-byte region is consistent with a cwd of `"/"`.

So a queued `source-file` (config re-source in this case) executed for a client that had already gone through `server_client_lost` — the client struct itself was still reachable from the command queue, but its `cwd` was already freed.

**Workload context**: the box was under rapid client attach/detach churn at the time (an external watchdog was kill/restarting the server and clients were auto-reattaching), so client lifetimes were unusually short relative to queued command execution. That presumably widened this race enough to hit it.

This is not the grid crash itself, but given the working theory that the grid corruption is fallout from a temporally-close UAF, a confirmed client-lifetime UAF on master seemed worth putting on this thread. Happy to move it to a separate issue if you prefer.

comments.author: participant3
reporter
comments.body:
The grid assert just fired here on latest master, this time with ASan **disabled** — posting since latest-master sightings were requested above.

**Build/env**: master `f07ea87e` (next-3.8), macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), arm64 (M-series). Same box and same commit as my cwd-UAF report above, but rebuilt with `--disable-asan` (overriding the darwin configure default), so this run is plain libmalloc.

**Crash**: SIGABRT via `__assert_rtn` in `grid_check_is_clear` (`grid_check_is_clear.cold.1`), on copy-mode entry, ~6h40m into server uptime (server started 08:23 local, aborted 15:05). Same entry path as the three crashes participant2 reported:

```
tmux  grid_check_is_clear.cold.1
tmux  grid_check_is_clear
tmux  grid_create
tmux  screen_init
tmux  window_copy_clone_screen
tmux  window_copy_init
tmux  window_pane_set_mode
tmux  cmd_copy_mode_exec
```

**Workload**: ordinary interactive use — 4 sessions / ~18 panes, several full-screen TUI apps redrawing continuously, wheel-up copy-mode entries throughout the day, `history-limit 10000` with several panes near the cap.

**Why this configuration seems like a useful data point**: with ASan disabled this is plain libmalloc with the zero-on-free semantics mentioned above — `grid_create` callocs the new grid, so the assert finding non-zero bytes means something wrote into a freed region between free and reuse (a write-after-free), not a stale-data artifact. It also matches the expectation that the assert can't fire under ASan (ASan's calloc really zeroes): the ASan build on this box never tripped this assert but caught the client-cwd UAF instead; the non-ASan build tripped it within ~7 hours.

Full .ips available on request.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
If you are running with ASAN disabled, set `MallocCheckZeroOnFreeCorruption=1` from that man page I shared. You might find more instances of write-after-free and it will report the data that was written, which might help figure out where it's coming from. 

Perhaps also `MallocCorruptionAbort=1`.

AFAIU, running with ASAN might still be helpful, since it might catch the write-after-free itself. I'm not sure which is more useful: ASAN or libmalloc with my suggestions above (but my suggestions should be better than just running with libmalloc).

One downside: once you run tmux server with those env vars set, the env vars will propagate to all programs using libmalloc that run inside tmux, which could slow something down or cause other programs to abort. I'm pretty sure tmux has a setting to remove an env var from pane environments, but I forget what it is.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
**TL;DR** — I have a self-contained reproducer for the `grid_check_is_clear` abort on `master` (a few minutes of scripted churn, plain libmalloc). When it fires, the freshly `xcalloc`'d `linedata` comes back holding the **intact, coherent contents of a previously-freed allocation** (an old grid's line array in some cases; a freed pane environment in others). I couldn't find a tmux-side use-after-free in the paths involved. So this looks like **`calloc` returning non-zeroed memory**, not a write scribbling on an already-zeroed page — though I can't fully exclude the latter. It also explains #4777 as the same bug seen one step later.

## Reproducer

`master 242239b5`, built `--enable-debug --disable-asan --enable-utf8proc` (plain libmalloc), macOS 26.5.1 (25F80) arm64. Point `TMUX_BIN` at your build:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -u
TMUX_BIN="${TMUX_BIN:-tmux}"
export TMUX_TMPDIR="${TMUX_TMPDIR:-/tmp/tmux5385}"; mkdir -p "$TMUX_TMPDIR"
S=r5385; GEN="$TMUX_TMPDIR/gen.sh"
cat > "$GEN" <<'G'
pad=$(printf '%.0sx' $(seq 1 300)); i=0
while true; do i=$((i+1)); w=$(( (i%240)+1 ))
  printf '\033[38;2;%d;%d;%dmL%06d %s\033[0m\n' $((i*7%256)) $((i*13%256)) $((i*29%256)) "$i" "${pad:0:$((w%300))}"
  (( i%5==0 )) && printf 'emoji \U0001F600 forces a wide/extended cell\n'  # optional; truecolor above already exercises extddata
  sleep 0.02
done
G
"$TMUX_BIN" -L$S kill-server 2>/dev/null; sleep 0.3
"$TMUX_BIN" -L$S new-session -d -s m -x 200 -y 50 "bash $GEN"
"$TMUX_BIN" -L$S set -g history-limit 50000
"$TMUX_BIN" -L$S set -g exit-empty off
"$TMUX_BIN" -L$S set -g window-size manual
"$TMUX_BIN" -L$S set-hook -g after-split-window 'resize-window -x 150 -y 40'
"$TMUX_BIN" -L$S set-hook -g window-linked     'resize-window -x 200 -y 50'
"$TMUX_BIN" -L$S split-window -t m "bash $GEN"
start=$SECONDS; r=0
while "$TMUX_BIN" -L$S has-session -t m 2>/dev/null; do
  r=$((r+1))
  "$TMUX_BIN" -L$S split-window -t m "bash $GEN" 2>/dev/null
  "$TMUX_BIN" -L$S break-pane -d 2>/dev/null
  "$TMUX_BIN" -L$S join-pane -s '{end}' 2>/dev/null
  "$TMUX_BIN" -L$S swap-pane -D 2>/dev/null
  "$TMUX_BIN" -L$S respawn-pane -k "bash $GEN" 2>/dev/null
  for p in $("$TMUX_BIN" -L$S list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id}' 2>/dev/null); do
    "$TMUX_BIN" -L$S copy-mode -e -t "$p" \; send-keys -t "$p" -X history-top \; \
      send-keys -t "$p" -X page-up \; send-keys -t "$p" -X cancel 2>/dev/null
  done
  n=$("$TMUX_BIN" -L$S list-panes -a 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  while [ "${n:-0}" -gt 8 ]; do
    lp=$("$TMUX_BIN" -L$S list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id}' 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
    [ -n "$lp" ] && "$TMUX_BIN" -L$S kill-pane -t "$lp" 2>/dev/null || break; n=$((n-1))
  done
  sleep 0.05
done
echo "server gone after $((SECONDS-start))s / $r rounds"
```

What matters: **pane-lifecycle churn** (`split` / `break-pane` / `join-pane` / `swap-pane` / `respawn-pane`) against **large scrollback** (`history-limit 50000`), with copy-mode entry every round. It aborts at copy-mode entry (`window_copy_clone_screen → grid_create → grid_check_is_clear`). Timing is stochastic — ~75 s to several minutes.

## What the corrupt `linedata` contains

I swapped the asserts in `grid_check_is_clear` for a routine that dumps the offending `grid_line` (+ neighbours) then zeroes it and continues, so one run harvests many samples. The corrupt region is never random — it's the **intact contents of a previously-freed allocation**, of two kinds:

1. **A former grid's line array** — runs of `grid_line` with a stale non-canonical `celldata` (e.g. `0x0002000000000000`), sequentially-spaced `extddata` heap pointers, and monotonically increasing `time`.
2. **A freed pane environment** — the block held a spawned pane's env strings (`TERM_PROGRAM`, terminal-emulator vars, `PATH`/`MANPATH`-type entries), i.e. the `struct environ` from `spawn_pane()` released by `environ_free()`.

Both are large `linedata` allocations (the clones that aborted here were ~0.6–1 MB). The workload constantly frees large `linedata` (killing/respawning big-history panes) then allocates a large clone `linedata` on copy-mode entry — and the freed block returns **not zeroed**, prior contents intact.

## Same root cause as #4777

The stale `celldata` is non-NULL garbage. On `master`, `grid_check_is_clear` asserts `celldata == NULL` and aborts first. Without it (3.7b), the clone is used and later freed, and `grid_free_line` does `free(gl->celldata)` on that garbage → *"pointer being freed was not allocated."* Same corruption, one step downstream — matching the 3.7b backtraces here.

## Why ASAN/tools miss it, and why it's erratic

- **ASAN**: doesn't reproduce at all (matches your note) — different recycling, and it zeroes `calloc`.
- **Reproduction rate is wildly state-dependent**: the *same* instrumented binary gave hundreds of detections in one window and **zero** in a comparable window an hour later. As I understand libmalloc, large frees go to a death-row cache / `madvise(MADV_FREE)` and are only reclaimed-and-zeroed under memory pressure — so whether a freed block is reused before it's reclaimed depends on pressure, which drifts. That would explain both the erraticness and why it only shows on stock libmalloc.

## Audit — no tmux use-after-free found

Since the corruption fingerprints the environ and grid-line free paths, I read them:

- `spawn_pane()` frees `child` exactly once (the forked child `execvp`s/`_exit`s without touching it); `cmd-respawn-pane.c` creates and frees `sc.environ` once; `environ_copy` is a deep copy. No UAF/double-free.
- `break-pane` / `swap-pane` / `join-pane` **move** panes (TAILQ / layout-cell / window pointers) and resize them — they never free a grid; `join-pane` removes the source pane before the empty-window kill. The only grid free is `screen_free(&wp->base)` in the refcounted `window_pane_free`. One free per pane.

(I didn't exhaustively audit every refcount path in the tree.)

## Where I land

Intact + coherent + *multi-type* stale contents, no UAF in the fingerprinted paths, and the memory-pressure-dependent erraticness together point at **`calloc` returning non-zeroed `linedata`** rather than a write-after-free on a zeroed page. `grid.c` relies on `xcalloc` (plain `calloc`) zeroing, and `grid_check_is_clear` is effectively checking that guarantee held — it doesn't.

I can't fully exclude a tmux WAF/overrun that dirties a block libmalloc thinks is zero (your original theory) — but surviving *original* contents fit non-zeroed reuse better than writer-supplied bytes.

If it's allocator-side, a cheap tmux mitigation is to not trust `calloc` zeroing for `linedata` (explicit `memset`, or make the macOS `grid_check_is_clear` path defensively zero instead of assert) — which would also cover #4777. Might be worth a Feedback Assistant report too; I couldn't find an existing public one. One data point that would help: do these crashes correlate with a specific macOS version? (zero-on-free / the large-cache behaviour is relatively recent.)

Happy to run a patch, a hardware-watchpoint recipe, or anything else against the reproducer.

comments.author: participant1

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
@participant1 had claude do a few more iterations. Not free for remainder of day but can take another look tm!

---
▎ Ran with MallocZeroOnFree=1 MallocCheckZeroOnFreeCorruption=1: no change — same grid_check_is_clear abort (2 crashes), and the malloc corruption check never fired.
▎
▎ Zone info added to the check (779 samples): the corrupt linedata is DefaultMallocZone, malloc_size 147456 or 229376 — 16 KB-page multiples, so the page-based large path, which presumably zero-on-free doesn't cover (consistent with the check staying silent). The stale celldata/extddata values are never live allocations (malloc_zone_from_ptr = no zone, malloc_size = 0 for all 1508 checked) — no aliasing; and on 3.7b freeing them is exactly "pointer being freed was not allocated" (#4777). The stale contents include tiny-zone debris (env strings, extd-entry-shaped records) inside the large block, so the reuse looks page-level, not block-level.
▎
▎ I also tried to reproduce the non-zeroed calloc standalone (correct-usage churn at the observed sizes, a deliberate UAF, cross-size churn, fork churn — ~1.3M checked callocs): all clean, while tmux reproduces in minutes. So it needs something in tmux's exact pattern — one difference I haven't isolated yet is that linedata lives through heavy incremental realloc growth (grid_scroll_history) before the free/calloc cycle.
▎
▎ Version correlation from the existing reports: every crash across #4777/#5140/#5267/#5385 is macOS 26 (26.1 → 26.5.2, Darwin 25); oldest is Dec 2025 on tmux 3.6a. Nothing pre-Tahoe. The .ips headers carry the version (os_version field) — #4777 has one pasted and #5267 one attached.

comments.body:
Follow-ups on jemalloc and the one loose end from my last comment:

**jemalloc fixes it.** `--enable-jemalloc` builds clean against Homebrew jemalloc 5.3.0 (`otool -L` shows `libjemalloc.2.dylib`) and runs fine. Ran 3 stock + 3 jemalloc-built servers simultaneously under identical churn for an hour: **stock crashed 3×, jemalloc 0**. An earlier 7-minute A/B with jemalloc preloaded via `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` (4+4 servers) gave the same differential: stock 3, jemalloc 0. Combined: stock 6 crashes, jemalloc 0, side by side on the same machine state.

**Realloc suspect closed:** I mimicked `grid_scroll_history`'s one-line-at-a-time growth standalone (12M reallocs to the observed sizes, dirtied, freed, calloc'd back, interleaved with tiny allocs) — clean. Also ran the whole churn inside a forked-never-exec'd child (the server's state per the ASI annotation), with continuous grandchild forks — clean. That's ~1.5M verified callocs across every pattern I could extract from tmux, all zero failures, while tmux itself reproduces in minutes. Consistent with your read: a macOS large-allocation bug that needs real accumulated allocator state, not a simple sequence.

(@participant3's Sequoia 15.7.7 negative fits the version picture — every crash on these threads is macOS 26. I'll give your `reallocprobe.c` a run on this Tahoe machine next — for what it's worth my own realloc-pattern probe above stayed clean here, so a standalone trigger may need more than that, but worth trying while a hot window is around.)

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Ran `reallocprobe.c` on the Tahoe machine that reproduces (100 reps/case, plus a variant calling `malloc_zone_pressure_relief()` between the free and the calloc): dirty 0 everywhere. The interesting number is `same_addr` ≈ 100/100 — calloc recycles the exact just-freed block every time, so the death-row path *is* exercised and zeroes correctly in isolation. Whatever breaks it needs accumulated state a short probe doesn't build. (Small note: `sizeof(struct grid_line)` is 40 on current master, not 56 — didn't change the outcome.)

Given that, the VM version-matrix may indeed be the practical route for an Apple report — though the tmux reproducer + zone data may already be enough to file.
